title: tailfold-latency-probe-log-harper
content:
Scratchpad: tailfold latency probe
Owner: Harper Nguyen (eng-serving-runtime)
Collaborators: Evan Brooks, Mira Joshi
Date range: 2025-10-05 -> 2025-11-02 (iterative runs)

Goal / Hypothesis:
- Investigate a "tailfold" idea: proactively preemption + short-term requeue of large-context, low-priority requests to reduce p99 for high-priority interactive traffic during microbursts.
- Hypothesis: modest preemption window (50-200ms) for low-priority jobs will reduce p99 by >30% with <5% increase in average completion time for preempted jobs.

Testbed:
- Cluster: dedicated small pool (4x A100s), sim infra on staging.
- Model: trimmed quantized t5-11B-like workload (sequence len 1->1024 mix, avg 196 tokens).
- Traffic mix: 80% HP interactive, 20% LP batch-ish. Arrival: synthetic Poisson with microburst overlays (3s bursts at 4x baseline QPS).
- Runtime options: continuous batching, KV cache warm, kernel selection default.

Key knobs tried:
- PF (preemption fraction): 0% (baseline), 10%, 25%, 50% of LP requests eligible for tailfolding.
- PW (preemption window): 0ms (baseline), 50ms, 100ms, 200ms.
- RB (requeue backoff): immediate enqueue, 50ms backoff, 200ms backoff.
- Priority lane capacity: HP lanes allowed to steal max 40% of LP slots during bursts.

Metrics captured (per run): p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies for HP and LP, throughput (QPS), LP average completion, LP retries, CPU/GPU utilization, observed batching efficiency (avg batch size).

Summary of runs (selected):
- Baseline (PF=0): HP p50=22ms p95=120ms p99=340ms, HP QPS at burst=820, LP avg=420ms, batch size avg=6.

- Run A (PF=10, PW=50, RB=50): HP p50=20ms p95=95ms p99=240ms, HP QPS=840, LP avg=460ms (+9.5%), LP retry=~8%, batch size avg=5.5. Observations: quick preemption helped HP tail; some fragmentation reduced batch size slightly.

- Run B (PF=25, PW=100, RB=50): HP p50=21ms p95=78ms p99=190ms, HP QPS=855, LP avg=520ms (+23.8%), LP retry=~16%, batch size avg=5.1. Observations: stronger p99 improvement, tradeoff noticeable on LP completion.

- Run C (PF=50, PW=200, RB=200): HP p50=23ms p95=68ms p99=145ms, HP QPS=870, LP avg=760ms (+81%), LP retry=~34%, batch size avg=4.4. Observations: best HP p99 but LP suffers; requeue backoff too long -> repeated preemptions and queue thrash.

- Run D (PF=25, PW=100, RB=200, steal-cap=40%): HP p50=22ms p95=82ms p99=165ms, HP QPS=860, LP avg=610ms (+45%), LP retry=~22%. Observation: introducing limit on steal-cap stabilized HP QPS but LP cost still high.

Quick ASCII trend (HP p99):
- baseline: 340ms
- A: 240ms
- B: 190ms
- C: 145ms
- D: 165ms

Quick ASCII trend (LP avg):
- baseline: 420ms
- A: 460ms
- B: 520ms
- C: 760ms
- D: 610ms

Latency distribution notes:
- Preemption reduces long tails effectively by cutting in-progress LP work mid-generation; HP requests get earlier GPU slots and smaller effective queue depth.
- But repeated preemption increases wasted compute (partial KV/cache warmups lost) and reduces effective batching (smaller average batch sizes).
- At extreme PF/PW values we introduce oscillatory behavior: LP replays congest the queue after the burst -> secondary tail for HP if replays coincide with next microburst window.

Operational concerns:
- Visibility: need to add tags in traces pointing to preempted requests (reason, attempts) for postmortem.
- Fairness: SLA for LP customers (background ingestion) — have to enforce max retries or TTL after which job auto-fails or moves to long-run queue.
- Cost: wasted cycles increase GPU cost per effective token; need to estimate ROI vs SLA benefit.

Next experiments to run (planned):
1) Soft checkpointing for LP requests at token boundaries (so preemption loses less progress) -> hypothesize LP avg penalty cut by ~40%.
2) Adaptive PF/PW driven by a probe meter (if HP latency rising > threshold, enable tailfold). Reduce steady-state LP impact.
3) Hybrid strategy: preempt only if predicted remaining tokens > X AND expected HP queue wait > Y. Use cheap model to predict remaining generation.
4) Measure across model families: longer-context models (16k) likely worse for LP when preempted.

Immediate recommendations (for prototyping):
- Implement RB=50ms + PF=25% + PW=100ms as default tailfold toggled only during detected microbursts. Add a soft cap on requeues per LP job = 2.
- Add tracing metadata and a dashboard slice for preempted-work overhead (GPU ms wasted, LP retries).
- Pilot on a small customer slice (internal) with opt-in LP jobs.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How will KV cache priming cost affect models with heavy prefix reuse? Preemption might lose high-value cache work.
- Interaction with continuous batching heuristics: can we re-batch preempted LP chunks without huge overhead?
- Scheduling fairness in multi-tenant dedicated pools vs single-tenant dedicated pools.

Notes to self:
- Save traces for Run B and C, correlate with batch composition snapshots.
- Run soft-checkpoint proto on 2025-11-05 with Mira.
- Draft Linear ticket for adaptive PF gating after initial dashboarding.

Attachments (local): staging-runB-traces.tar.gz, batch-composition-runC.csv, quickplots/tailfold_hp_p99.png

End of scratchpad.
